transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess what made me come in is my eating. After really long days on site, or sometimes after a neighborhood meeting, I’ll get home and just eat way more than I meant to. Like leftover takeout, cereal, chips—whatever’s around. I keep going until I’m uncomfortably full, and it’s been bothering me.
Do you usually feel guilty after these episodes of eating too much?
I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I do feel bad about it sometimes, like frustrated with myself, but I don’t know if I’d call it guilt every time.
Do these episodes of eating too much happen regularly?

Yeah, I’d say it’s regular. Looking back over the last few months, it averages out to about once a week. Some weeks it might happen twice, and then another week maybe not at all, but overall it’s been about weekly.
During these episodes of eating too much, do you feel like you're unable to stop or control how much you're eating?

Yeah. Once I start on those nights, it feels kind of like I’m on autopilot. I’ll be thinking, “I need to stop, I have an early crew start,” but then I still end up going back into the kitchen for more.
Do you ever feel a lack of control over your eating during these episodes without feeling guilty afterwards?

Yeah, that happens. The main thing is the loss of control — like once I start, I feel like I’m on autopilot. I’ll tell myself I need to stop because I have an early crew start, but I still end up going back to the kitchen for more.
Do you usually feel very hungry before these episodes of eating too much?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed that I’m especially hungry beforehand every time. Sometimes I might be hungry, but I don’t think that’s the main thing I’m aware of.
Do you usually eat more when you're stressed or emotional?

Yeah, I think so. It’s usually after a really long day on site, or sometimes after a neighborhood meeting that’s stressful. I’ll get home and just start eating whatever’s around — leftover takeout, cereal, chips — and it ends up being way more than I meant to, to the point where I’m uncomfortably full.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?
I’m not really sure. I don’t weigh myself that often, and I haven’t noticed a major change in how my clothes fit or anything.
Do you think you eat more when you're feeling emotional as a way to calm down or feel better?

Yeah, I think that’s part of it. After a long day on site or a stressful meeting, I’ll get home and just start eating whatever’s there — leftovers, cereal, chips — and it feels like I’m trying to settle down somehow. But then I end up eating way more than I meant to, until I’m really uncomfortably full.
Do you ever eat when you're feeling empty inside, not necessarily because you're hungry?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think of it as feeling “empty inside.” It’s more like I’m stressed or worn out, and then I eat without really planning to.
Do you usually eat more when you're feeling anxious or upset?

Yeah, usually after I’m anxious or upset from work or a neighborhood meeting. I’ll get home and just eat whatever’s around — like leftover takeout, cereal, chips — and it turns into way more than I meant to. I don’t really stop until I’m uncomfortably full.
Do you ever feel like eating is a way to fill an emotional void, rather than just being hungry?

I don’t know if I’d call it an emotional void. That doesn’t really sound like how I think about it. It feels more like I’m tense or drained, and eating is just… what I end up doing. Not always because I’m actually hungry, but I’m not sure it’s about filling something.
Do you feel like eating helps you deal with feelings of emptiness or hollowness inside?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it as “emptiness” or hollowness exactly. It’s more that I feel stressed or kind of worn out, and then I end up eating. I don’t think of it as fixing an empty feeling.
Have you ever made yourself vomit or used laxatives after one of these episodes of eating too much?

Yes. Not every time, but a few times a month after those nights, I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. I get panicky about what I ate and about undoing all the work I put into looking put-together.
How often do you make yourself vomit after one of these episodes of eating too much?
A few times a month, usually after those nights where I feel like I ate way too much. I’ll get really panicky about it and go make myself throw up.
Do you make yourself vomit or use laxatives after every episode of eating too much, or is it less often than that?

It’s less often than that. I don’t do it after every time I overeat. It’s more like a few times a month, usually when I really panic afterward and feel like I need to undo it, so I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up.
Do you make yourself vomit or use laxatives after most episodes of eating too much?
No, not most of them. It’s only a few times a month, usually after those nights when I panic about what I ate. Then I’ll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up, like I’m trying to undo it.
Do you make yourself vomit or use laxatives after more than half of your episodes of eating too much?
No, not more than half. It’s just a few times a month, usually after those nights when I panic and feel like I have to undo it, so I make myself throw up.
Do you make yourself vomit or use laxatives after almost all of your episodes of eating too much?

No, not almost all of them. Like I said, it’s only a few times a month. It’s usually after those nights where I really panic and feel like I need to undo it, so I go to the bathroom and make myself throw up.
Do you make yourself vomit or use laxatives after at least half of your episodes of eating too much?

No, not at least half. It’s more like a few times a month after those bad nights. I’ll panic about undoing all the work I’ve put into looking put-together, and then I go to the bathroom and make myself throw up.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits recurrent episodes of eating significantly more food in a short period of time than most people would eat under similar circumstances, with episodes marked by feelings of lack of control. The patient also engages in inappropriate compensatory behaviors, such as self-induced vomiting, although not after every episode, indicating a pattern of behavior that aligns more closely with Other Specified Feeding or Eating Disorder (OSFED), given the frequency and characteristics of the behaviors.
